title: Mike LaFleur Press Conference: September 28, 2026
headline: No injuries reported, but LaFleur is frustrated with a lack of explosive plays and self-inflicted penalties, and he praised LB Jack Gibbens.
summary: LaFleur said the offense has been efficient for most of the season but needs more explosive plays. He attributed the lack of big gains to a mix of blocking details, receivers not getting connected, and checkdowns, rather than to any one player. He said the penalties, especially three pre-snap and post-snap penalties on the first three drives, were a team-wide problem that put the offense in a hole. On defense, he said the team's play style is right but it needs clarity and cleaner execution on blitz timing, fronts, and tackling. He called the run blocking better but still full of busts, and he took responsibility for them as a coaching issue. He said there were no injuries from the game. He praised Marvin Harrison Jr.'s route-running and said he is looking forward to working with him again on Wednesday. He is also pleased with special teams, though he wants more. He praised Gibbens as a strong addition to the defense. The next opponent is New York, and LaFleur said the focus is on his own team, with situational adjustments for the opposing quarterback.

title: Jesse Minter Recaps Ravens' Thrilling Win Over Cowboys
headline: Ravens' Ioane stepped in at center in a late-game spot and is getting backup reps; Gwyn's injury status remains unclear after the 34-31 win over Dallas.
summary: Minter praised the Cowboys as a strong team and said the Ravens' 34-31 win came down to the final seconds, with the defense failing to finish the game cleanly over the last quarter. He credited the defense for holding Dallas to a field goal after it had first-and-goal at the one. He said the offense hit a key play with seven seconds left, which he called unbelievable work by Lamar Jackson and Zay Flowers, and he added that the team was ready for that situation. On the field conditions, he said the team did not let the surface bother them and the field held up well. He called Roquan Smith the team's leader for the big first-half sack and for his role directing the defense. Minter said the offense left some points on the table by going for touchdowns on fourth down instead of settling for field goals, and that the team wants to separate earlier in close games. On the injury front, he had no update on Jovaughn Gwyn and said the team would wait and see. He praised Olaivavega Ioane for stepping in at center in a key moment and said the team has been giving him some reps there. He also described the clock-management decision, noting that a touchback after the final seven seconds placed the ball at the 35, and said the team practices these moments.

title: Joe Brady Reflects On Bills Win And Performance Against The Chargers
headline: Bills' Ray Davis is set to get more backfield work as Ty Johnson returns, Greg Rousseau is playing with confidence, and Christian Benford's injury status is still unclear.
summary: Brady said the medical staff will evaluate the bumps and bruises over the next few days, and he is not concerned about Josh Allen's usual day-after soreness. He praised Maxwell Hairston and Davison Igbinosun for handling their reps in outside cornerback, saying the more reps they get, the better for the team, and that he will never be confident with a particular 11 on the field. On ball security, he said the team must be more intentional about how it goes to the ground and covers the ball, and that the turnovers were within its control. He defended the defense's third-down performance, but said the first and second down efforts drive third-down results, and he said the team has to clean up tackling in the open field. He said the defense improved in its run fits and gap discipline, and the goal-line plan is complex but the team is handling it. Brady said Ty Johnson's return brings a unique dynamic and gave him full trust, and he wants to get Ray Davis more touches going forward. He said the fourth-down decisions were aggressive and not hesitant, and he credited Keon Coleman for making plays even without the stat line. Finally, he credited Bradley Chubb's leadership for Greg Rousseau's confident play and said the outside linebacker rotation will continue to be managed to keep players fresh.

Akayleb Evans filled in well at cornerback, Chau Smith-Wade will step into the rotation, and the team may elevate Corey Thornton from the practice squad while looking for other options. Bryce Young was sore after taking a cleat to the ankle; Canales wants to check it further but expects him to play Sunday night against the Lions.

On injuries, he reported no lingering effects for Watson from a fourth-quarter hit and said Tytus Howard has been playing through nicks and bruises. Tyson Campbell was close to going in the game, and Monken feels good about him for Thursday. Dawand Jones has worked at both tackle spots, mostly right tackle lately, and is ready to step in. Monken said the team will have a better read on post-game health over the next day or two, and he would have an update on the knee injury involving a player named Tyler later in the day. On Denzel Boston, he admitted the team can move him around more and stack plays to get him more targets, and called the low target count partly a byproduct of game flow and protection. He praised Quincy Williams for playing faster and more comfortable in the system, and credited Denzel Ward and Grant Delpit for their play. The team's next game is a Thursday night contest.

title: HC Sean Payton on Broncos’ win over Rams: ‘Really, a tale of two halves’
headline: Payton credits a more balanced second-half offense for the comeback win, gives Talanoa Hufanga the game ball, and says Marvin Mims Jr. is hoped to return soon.
summary: Payton called the 30-26 win over the Rams a gutsy result and described it as a tale of two halves, with the first half going badly for the defense and offense. He said the second half improved mainly because the offense ran the ball effectively, stayed on schedule, got some big plays, and took pressure off Bo Nix. He admitted the first half was rough, citing a 13-point deficit and a two-minute drive that ended in a field goal, and said getting off to faster starts is the team's biggest issue. He praised Talanoa Hufanga for his pick-six and consistent leadership, saying he gets the game ball even though he had already received similar recognition. On the two-point tries, Payton said the 16-6 score made the conversion attempt the right call, and he would have kicked had the game been higher-scoring. He also said a young new returner had his first game and that the kickoff penalty and re-kick hurt field position. He hopes Marvin Mims Jr. can return soon, and he said he is comfortable with the team's fourth-quarter grit but not with its slow starts.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Titans' first-half offense has stalled in all three games due to drops and inefficiency; Saleh defended Cam Ward's decision-making, praised Jeffery Simmons, and left Carmona and Slater's injuries unresolved.
summary: Saleh said the offense has been slow to start in all three games, with drops on early downs and third downs, a lack of precision, and inefficiency that he wants corrected. He felt the team was robbed of a drive extension on a missed call for forward progress. He defended Cam Ward, saying he is decisive and generally takes care of the ball, and called his last-play decision a bad one rather than a reckless one. Saleh pointed to strong second-half efficiency and EPA numbers, while calling the first half 'abysmal.' He defended the choice to go for it on fourth down instead of kicking a field goal, citing kicker Joey Slye's reliability and the limited possessions left. He praised Jeffery Simmons as elite and said he deserves defensive player of the week consideration. Saleh also said Gunnar Helm could earn more red-zone work but has to earn it. Injury updates were limited to Fernando Carmona and Jackson Slater, who are both still being evaluated, with Slater finishing the game despite a significant foot injury.

title: HC Dan Quinn | 09/29/26
headline: Marcus Mariota is running the offense with Jayden Daniels still in a return-to-play process; Rachaad White, Samuel Cosmi, and Nick Cross are all still uncertain for the coming week.
summary: Quinn opened with an update on Leo Chenal, who had surgery that morning that went well, and said the team is encouraged by the reports. He said Jayden Daniels, Frankie Luvu, and Chig Okonkwo should all return to practice in some form this week. Daniels is working through a structured return-to-play process, with a lighter Wednesday and the bigger ramp-up coming Thursday, and a full-go decision is not yet made. Samuel Cosmi's travel status depends on further testing, with an update expected Tuesday. Quinn praised Mariota and Terry McLaurin for their in-game play, and said Mariota and the offense were in sync at the line with audibles. He also said Rachaad White showed toughness finishing the game despite a shoulder injury, and that Thursday and Friday will be his biggest test. On Lucas Patrick, Quinn said the new interior lineman was tough through a foot injury and the team wanted to keep balance in the run game. Austin Ekeler is expected to travel and will be integrated into a new offensive system over the next few days. Quinn said there is no update yet on Nick Cross's ability to travel to London or practice.
